title: Systemd Error: status=203/EXEC (Service Failed to Start)
symptoms: No such file or directory in ExecStart
root_cause: Systemd cannot execute the command specified in ExecStart. Common causes include: a typo in the binary path, missing execution permissions (+x), a missing script interpreter (e.g. #!/bin/bash or #!/usr/bin/env python3), Windows CRLF line endings in the script, or SELinux/AppArmor blocking execution.
diagnostic_steps: Check the ExecStart line in the unit file: systemctl cat <service_name>
Verify the executable path exists and has executable permissions: ls -l /path/to/binary
Check the shebang line if it is a script: head -n 1 /path/to/script
Check for Windows carriage returns: file /path/to/script (look for 'CRLF line terminators')
remediation_commands: sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart <service_name>

title: Systemd Error: status=217/USER (Failed at Step USER Spawning)
root_cause: The service unit file specifies a 'User=' or 'Group=' directive with a username or group that does not exist on the system.
diagnostic_steps: Inspect the User and Group directives: grep -E '^(User|Group)=' /etc/systemd/system/<service_name>.service
Verify if the user exists: id <configured_user>
remediation_commands: sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart <service_name>

title: Systemd Error: Start Request Repeated Too Quickly (Start-Limit-Hit)
root_cause: The service has Restart=always or Restart=on-failure configured and crashed multiple times within the StartLimitIntervalSec window (default is usually 5 starts within 10 seconds). Systemd stops restarting to prevent infinite crash loops.
diagnostic_steps: Check the exact application crash logs: journalctl -u <service_name> -n 50 --no-pager
Check the service configuration: systemctl show <service_name> -p StartLimitIntervalSec,StartLimitBurst
remediation_commands: sudo systemctl reset-failed <service_name>  # Clears the start rate limit counter
# Fix the underlying application crash seen in journalctl

title: Systemd Error: status=1/FAILURE (Application Crash on Startup)
symptoms: Service exited with general failure code
root_cause: The binary executed successfully, but the application itself encountered an unhandled exception, syntax error, missing environment variable, or configuration error and terminated with return code 1.
diagnostic_steps: View application stderr in journal: journalctl -u <service_name> -e -n 40
Test running the ExecStart command directly in the terminal as the service user to reproduce the crash
remediation_commands: # Check configuration file syntax (e.g. nginx -t or apachectl configtest)
# Verify environment file permissions and syntax if EnvironmentFile= is used
